2609.06085.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Price-Trade Dynamics: From Black-Box Forecasts to Effective Parametric Models
2609.06085.paper_summary: Understanding the joint dynamics of prices and trades is central to market microstructure, where returns and order flow interact through nonlinear and state-dependent mechanisms. Linear models are interpretable but may miss these effects, while deep neural networks improve forecasting at the cost of transparency. We use neural networks as tools for structural discovery rather than only for prediction. A deep feed-forward network is trained on high-frequency returns and signed volumes for large- and small-tick stocks and compared with a linear VAR benchmark. The neural network improves predictive performance, especially for returns, revealing nonlinear dependencies beyond the linear specification. Using Shapley-based explainability, we show that the dominant contributions are concentrated at the most recent lags. Model-implied responses are consistent with conditional averages reconstructed from the data. Unlike empirical averages, however, the neural-network decomposition isolates individual regressor contributions to the aggregate dependence. Lagged signed volume generates sign-preserving and saturating effects, consistent with nonlinear price impact and order-flow persistence. Lagged returns act as state variables: when the previous trade does not move the price, the model predicts continuation in the direction of past order flow, whereas non-zero returns generate attenuation or reversal. Building on these findings, we introduce a parsimonious SHAP-inspired nonlinear parametric model. It reproduces the main return-volume dependencies, outperforms the linear VAR benchmark, and achieves performance comparable to the neural network. A multi-lag extension captures residual longer-memory effects while preserving interpretability. Overall, explainability offers a route from black-box prediction to economically meaningful parametric models of price and trade dynamics.
2609.06085.paper_summary_zh: 理解價格與交易的聯合動態對於市場微觀結構至關重要，回報與訂單流通過非線性和狀態依賴的機制相互作用。線性模型是可解釋的，但可能會忽略這些效應，而深度神經網絡在提高預測能力的同時，犧牲了透明度。我們將神經網絡用作結構發現的工具，而不僅僅是用於預測。深度前饋網絡在高頻回報和簽名交易量上進行訓練，針對大幅度和小幅度股票，並與線性VAR基準進行比較。神經網絡提高了預測性能，特別是在回報方面，揭示了超越線性規範的非線性依賴性。利用基於Shapley的可解釋性，我們顯示出主要貢獻集中在最新的滯後期。模型所暗示的反應與從數據重建的條件平均值一致。然而，與經驗平均值不同，神經網絡分解能夠隔離對總體依賴的個別回歸變數貢獻。滯後的簽名交易量產生保留符號和飽和效應，與非線性價格影響和訂單流持續性一致。滯後回報作為狀態變數：當前一筆交易未能移動價格時，模型預測將沿著過去的訂單流方向持續，而非零回報則產生衰減或反轉。基於這些發現，我們引入了一個簡約的受SHAP啟發的非線性參數模型。它再現了主要的回報-交易量依賴性，表現超過線性VAR基準，並達到與神經網絡相當的性能。一個多滯後擴展捕捉剩餘的長期記憶效應，同時保持可解釋性。總體而言，可解釋性提供了一條從黑箱預測到經濟上有意義的價格與交易動態參數模型的途徑。
2609.06085.author: Manuel Naviglio et.al.
